newsitem.title: UK: Charts show Italian BTPs at risk after ERM move.
newsitem.headline: Charts show Italian BTPs at risk after ERM move.

text.p: Italian BTP futures are vulnerable to a considerable slide lower after the lira made its move back into Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) on Sunday, technical analysts said on Monday.
Daily price action charts show the market has made a distinct top at 128.58, its contract high, and is unlikely to sustain the accelerated bull run which has gripped the market since August.
"The market is extremely volatile in this current environment," said Tom Hobson at Merrill Lynch in London.
December BTP futures started Monday's session weaker, dipping to a low at 127.48 in early trade before recovering slightly. By 0824 GMT, the contract was four basis points down on the day at 127.88.
Chartists said a move up towards the contract high at 128.58 -- set on November 20 -- would be possible in the short term, but said investors should be cautious beyond there.
"We're on "reversal watch' with this market at the moment," said David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse in London.
Sneddon said signs late last week that the direction of lira and the BTP contract were diverging constituted a clear warning.
"Mark/lira has declined, and the BTP has come up but not really penetrated very much," he said.
"Looking at the BTP on a long-term charts, it really looks as if this is quite an unsustainable move," he said.
December BTPs have staged a sharp rally since August, putting on several major spurts of accelerated gains.
Chartists said the speed of the move undermined its strength, and suggested that any technical break lower would spark a sharp decline in BTP prices.
Analysts said one key point for a possible break lower was the 128.50 to 127.56 area.

"If we came back below the 127.55 hourly pivot region, that would certainly suggest an immediate loss of upside momentum," said Sneddon. "Then the market could come back and challenge its recent lows."
Technical analysts pointed to 126.62, the low plotted on daily charts on November 22, as further support, but said the risk of further sharp declines was looming.
Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data, said things looked dangerous for BTPs below 127.56.
"Below 127.56, there is really not very much in the way of support until we get to the 125.00 area," said Diebel. "And that is a long way down."
While chartists said the chance of some sort of upside move was still there for BTPs, they said investors should tread very carefully.
"If the market continues to rally quickly, we may take some profits 20 to 30 basis points higher than we are now," Hobson, Merrill's director of technical analysis, told Reuters Financial Television.
Credit Suisse's Sneddon agreed.
"The greatest luxury would be not to have to be in this market at all," he said. "But certainly, if I had to be long, I would be long with very careful stops."
-- Kate Kelland, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 8682
